VIỆT-NAM DÂN CHỦ CỘNG HÒA
—
C ÍNH PHỦ LÂM THỜI
—
BO NGOAI GIAO
*
125
later found in keeping with San Francisco
Charter and which has been fully carried out
these last years: continuous fight against
the Japanese bringing about the recovery of
national independence on August 19th, volunt-
ary abdication of Ex-Emperor Baodai, establish-
ment of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam, assist-
ance given to the Allies Nations in the disarmament
of the Japanese, appointment of a provisional
Government whose mission was to carry out the
Atlantic and San Francisco Charters and have them
carried out by other nations.

As a matter of fact, the carrying out of the
Atlantic and San Francisco Charters implies the
eradication of imperialism and all forms of colonial
oppression. This was unfortunately contrary to the
interests of some Frenchmen, and France, to whom the
colonists have long concealed the truth on Indo-
china, instead of entering into peaceable negotiatie
ions , resorted to an aggressive invasion,
with all the means at the command of a modern nation.
Moreover, having persuaded the British that the
Vietnamese are wishing for a return of the French
rule, they obtained, first from the British command
in South East Asia, then from London, a tacit
recognition of their sovereignty and administrative
responsibility as far as South Vietnam is concerned.
The British gave to understand that they had agreed
to this on the ground that the reestablishment of
French administration and, consequently, of Franco-
Vietnamese collaboration would help them to speed
up the demobilization and the disarmament of the
Japanese. But subsequent events will prove the
fallacy of the argument. The whole Vietnamese nation
rose up as one man against French aggression. The
first street-sniping which was launched by the
French in the small hours of September 23rd soon
developed into real and organized warfare in which
losses are heavy on both sides. The bringing in of
French important reinforcements on board of the most
powerful of their remaining warships will extend the
war zone further. As murderous fighting is still
going on in Indonesia, and as savage acts on the
part of Frenchmen are reported every day, we may
expect the flaring up of a general conflagration
in the Far-East.

As it is, the situation in South Vietnam calls
for immediate interference. The establishment of
the Consultative Commission for the Far-East has
been enthusiastically welcomed here as the first
effective........

Franklin D. Roosevelt
Vice President
FIDELITY AND DEPOSIT COMPANY OF MARYLAND
55 Liberty Street New York City
at Warm Springs, Georgia,
April 8, 1927.
Dear Julian:
I do hope you can manage to get down here some-
time before I go back to New York the first week in May.
Things are coming along well and the new Patients' Pool
[…]t ready. There is no question that we shall have
[…]e applications from patients than we have accommo-
for, and the only trouble is that so many of them
[…]ally poor people who cannot afford to pay the actual
[…]f $42 a week. I am starting a Patients' Aid Fund to
[…]ese poor children and hope to be able to assist
[…]15 out of the 50 patients.
Did I tell you that I have completely separated
[…]wo portions of the property - hotel, cottages and
[…]ients pools to be owned and run by a membership corpora-
[…]n - non-profit making and financed entirely by gifts
and by the small actual cost rate charged to the patients.
All the rest of the property goes into the Meriwether
Reserve, and develops the golf course, cottage colony, etc.,
and this also, when the development cost is paid back, will
have its profits go to the Foundation.
Meanwhile, lots of people are becoming interested
in the place and its future looks very bright.
Always sincerely yours,
Franklin D Roosevelt

S.G.O.201-Leonard, Esther E.,
MCG.
WAR DEPARTMENT
OFFICE OF THE SURGEON GENERAL
WASHINGTON
May 18, 1918.
Dr. Esther E. Leonard,
6410A Michigan Avenue,
St. Louis, Missouri.
Madam:-
I am directed by the Surgeon General to inclose herewith con-
tract which should be dated and signed by you in the presence of a
witness, whose signature should appear on the line provided there-
for, and be returned to this office, in the inclosed franked envel-
ope. No contract should be returned addressed to any person other
than "The Surgeon General, U. S. Army." One copy of the contract
[…]uld be retained by you.
[…]u will note that the contract covers a period of one month.
[…]es not imply that it will necessarily terminate at the end
[…] period. It can be continued indefinitely if such exten-
[…]s mutually agreeable.
Immediately upon signing this contract you should telegraph
[…]ffice that you have done so, when steps will be taken to have
[…]perly placed on duty.
[…] not enter upon your duties, nor perform any travel under
[…]contract until you have received from The Adjutant General of
[…]rmy, either by telegraph or mail, an order to do so.
Seven cents per mile is allowed as commutation for travel per-
[…]ed under proper orders, and upon the completion of any such trav-
[…]mileage voucher should be obtained from the nearest Quartermaster,
[…]n you should fill in, making no extension in the money column how-
[…]r, and then return the same together with two copies of the order
[…]ecting the travel, to the Quartermaster for payment.
At the end of each month during your service under your contract,
you should obtain pay voucher from the nearest Quartermaster and re -
turn it properly prepared, together with your copy of contract, which
will be returned to you by the Quartermaster after he has made nota-
tion of payment thereon.
Just as soon as you have completed the duties for which your con-
tract was made, and have returned to your home under proper orders, you
should notify this office of that fact by telegraph, when your contract
will be annulled.
C. W. AYARS
Major, Sanitary Corps, N. A.
